text:
St. Louis gave Anaheim two first-round picks, Nos. 15 and 29, for Mason McTavish in June, and The Hockey News already has him in a headline about players who "have gone cold since hot starts to Blues career." The point totals back that up: 3 points in his last ten games, where our numbers expected about 6.

The chances say otherwise. McTavish is generating 1.59 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his shots), up from 1.22 in Anaheim. He has 52 shots in 19 games and 8.2 expected goals behind his 7 real ones. The Blues have also put him on the ice for 65% of their power-play chances, up from 36% last season. His linemates have finished about three goals below their chances, which is where the missing assists went.

The concern is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting much more with him on the ice last season (bottom 2% of forwards), even as he helped drive play. This season St. Louis is about even on chances with him out there. If that holds, the cold spell is a finishing slump, not a role problem.
